answer: DeepWalk performs poorly on the language network because its random-walk/skip-gram objective mainly captures local co-occurrence patterns and is less effective when the graph has strong edge-weight or edge-type structure that matters for preserving the network’s semantics. In contrast, the LINE variants are designed to model first-order and second-order proximity more directly, so they fit this kind of network better. LINE needs to handle the edges’ weights effectively, since the strength/frequency of connections is important for learning a good embedding.
